name: Primary Polyarteritis Nodosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American College of Rheumatology 1990 Criteria for Polyarteritis Nodosa

criteria.description: Unexplained weight loss greater than 4 kg
Livedo reticularis or other skin manifestations of vasculitis
Diastolic blood pressure greater than 90 mm Hg
Elevated blood urea nitrogen or creatinine unrelated to dehydration or obstruction
Hepatitis B virus surface antigen positive
Arteriographic abnormalities (aneurysms or occlusions of visceral arteries)
Biopsy of small- or medium-sized artery containing polymorphonuclear cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least 3 of the above criteria including either biopsy or angiographic abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other vasculitides and secondary causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Microaneurysms of medium-sized arteries on angiography
searchTerms: small artery bulges seen on angiogram

common.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain due to mesenteric ischemia
searchTerms: belly pain from poor blood flow
abdominal pain due to low intestine blood supply

occasional.symptomName: Elevated blood pressure without renal artery stenosis
searchTerms: high blood pressure without kidney artery narrowing
elevated blood pressure not caused by renal artery blockage

rare.symptomName: Myocardial infarction due to coronary arteritis
searchTerms: heart attack from coronary artery inflammation
myocardial infarction due to artery swelling

rare.symptomName: Stroke secondary to cerebral artery involvement
searchTerms: stroke caused by brain artery disease
brain blood vessel blockage leading to stroke

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in renal involvement
Hepatitis B surface antigen positivity in some cases
imaging: Angiography showing microaneurysms and stenoses of medium-sized arteries
CT angiography or MR angiography confirming vessel abnormalities
other: Histopathology showing transmural necrotizing inflammation of medium-sized arteries with fibrinoid necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Involves small vessels rather than medium-sized arteries
Predominantly affects large vessels (aorta and branches)
Temporal artery tenderness and elevated ESR
Palpable purpura and renal involvement with hematuria

redFlags: Severe abdominal pain with signs of bowel ischemia
Mononeuritis multiplex with progressive neurological deficits
references: American College of Rheumatology 1990 Criteria for Polyarteritis Nodosa
